title: Act 3 (Final 5 Minutes of a Close Game): Pure Tension and Every-Possession Focus
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Final 5:00 of the 2nd Half or Overtime): The score is close (within a few baskets) and every single trip down the court can decide the winner.
editor_action: Eliminate distractions during live play: stay locked on the wide camera so viewers see defenders pressing full-court and players fighting to get open. Save all close-ups, slow-motion replays, and graphics strictly for moments when the game clock is completely stopped, focusing the bottom scoreboard on timeouts left and foul counts.
timing_constraint: Zero unnecessary cutaways while the ball is live in the final minutes; reserve all replays and close-ups for stopped-clock whistles (example: final 5:00 close-game mode) (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Master 5-Tier Control-Room Priority Hierarchy (Who Wins When Agents Collide)
trigger_condition: Multiple agents request the screen at the exact same moment (for example, after a basket-and-foul where Director wants a close-up, Replay wants slow-mo, and Graphics wants two stat banners).
editor_action: Arbitrate conflicts using a strict 5-tier priority ladder: (1) Live Ball in Play or Court Safety Lock on CAM-1 (Main Wide) always wins first > (2) Referee Foul/Violation Hand Signal > (3) Live Player or Coach Reaction (CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-4 (Coach & Bench)) > (4) Slow-Motion Replay (REPLAY-A) > (5) Lower-Third Stat Banner (GFX).
timing_constraint: Evaluate priority arbitration every 0.2s; higher-tier events immediately preempt or delay lower-tier requests.

title: Low Ball-Tracking Confidence Fallback (Safe Default to Wide CAM-1)
trigger_condition: A loose-ball pileup on the floor, a deflected rebound in traffic, or arena strobe lighting causes automated ball-tracking confidence to drop below the safety threshold.
editor_action: Whenever the system is momentarily unsure which player has the basketball, freeze all close-up camera switches and lock onto CAM-1 (Main Wide) with a wide zoom so the viewer at home can see the entire court scramble clearly.
timing_constraint: Lock CAM-1 Wide immediately whenever ball-tracking confidence drops below safety threshold (example: <65% tracker confidence).
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Unexpected Backcourt Steal Instant Bailout ('Never Miss a Live Basket' Guarantee)
trigger_condition: A close-up camera (CAM-3), coach camera (CAM-4), or slow-motion replay (REPLAY-A) is on screen during what looks like a routine walk-up inbound, and a defender suddenly steals or deflects the inbound pass near the basket.
editor_action: Immediately interrupt any close-up, coach shot, or replay with a sub-second emergency cut back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) and restore the scoreboard so the viewer never misses a surprise steal and layup.
timing_constraint: Preempt any non-CAM-1 feed within a sub-second emergency window on backcourt steals or deflections (example: <0.4s bailout to CAM-1).
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Late Return from Commercial Emergency Catch-Up Rule
trigger_condition: A commercial break runs two seconds long and the live game feed returns just as a player is already shooting or scoring on the court. (Visual cue: Ball already live in the frontcourt at the moment the commercial fades out; Audio cue: Play-by-play announcer immediately jumping into live action without a promo read.)
editor_action: If a commercial return arrives with live action already underway, bypass all return bumpers, theme music, promo reads, and replay packages, cutting 100% directly to CAM-1 (Main Wide) with the scorebug visible on frame zero (example: instant zero-delay cut to CAM-1 (Main Wide) if game clock is already running). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Never roll a recorded replay clip coming out of a commercial break if the live ball is already in play (Complete transition >= 3.0s before referee hands ball to inbounder.)

title: Master Safe-Harbor Rule: When in Any Doubt, Cut to Camera 1 Wide
trigger_condition: Any multi-agent conflict, low-confidence visual detection (< 0.75), unexpected whistle, camera obstruction, or timing desynchronization occurs. (Visual cue: Ambiguous or rapidly changing court state; Audio cue: Uncertain or overlapping audio cues.)
editor_action: Treat the Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide) with the compact scorebug as the universal safe-harbor state of the broadcast: whenever any agent encounters low confidence, sensor noise, or conflicting signals, default immediately to CAM-1 (Main Wide) until certainty is restored (example: CAM-1 (Main Wide) fallback whenever confidence < 0.75). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: A viewer can always follow and enjoy a basketball game from CAM-1 (Main Wide), whereas a wrong tight cut can cause them to miss the decisive play of the game (Trigger safe-harbor fallback to CAM-1 Wide within < 0.5s of confidence drop.)

title: End-Of-Game Close Score Lockout (Staying Wide Under Full-Court Pressure)
trigger_condition: The final minutes of the second half or overtime when the score is very close, or whenever defenders guard the offense across the entire length of the court ('full-court press').
editor_action: Keep the broadcast locked on CAM-1 (Main Wide) immediately after a made basket so viewers can see if defenders steal the pass coming back into play. Skip non-essential replays until a full timeout is called.
timing_constraint: Prioritize uninterrupted full-court visibility over celebration close-ups whenever defenders pressure the inbound pass (example: sub-second 0.8s glance or continuous wide hold).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Act 1 (Opening 5 Minutes): Helping Viewers Learn Who Is Who and Which Way Each Team Is Going
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (First 5 Minutes of the Game): The opening stretch after the center-court jump ball ('tip-off').
editor_action: Hold the wide camera longer than usual during the first few minutes so viewers can get comfortable with jersey colors, court direction, and team styles (whether a team likes to shoot from far away or pass inside near the tall players). Use the first few whistle pauses to introduce each team's starting five players and season records.
timing_constraint: Calmer camera switching pace during the opening 5 minutes of game clock to orient the audience before accelerating cut tempo (example: ~7 to 8 cuts per minute).

title: Telling Apart a Quick 2-Second Whistle from a Long 10-Second Stoppage
trigger_condition: The referee blows the whistle to stop the game clock, and the control room must decide whether there is enough time for a replay or stat banner.
editor_action: Measure what kind of whistle just happened: if the ball simply went out of bounds with no substitutions, play will resume in about 2 to 3 seconds, so keep the wide camera on screen and block all replays and banners. If a shooting foul, substitution horn, or timeout occurred, play will pause for 8 to 30+ seconds, opening the window for replays and graphics.
timing_constraint: Stay live and wide on quick stoppages (example: 2s to 3s throw-in); only trigger replays or banners on extended pauses (example: 8s+ foul or substitution).
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: End-Of-Half and Final Buzzer Sequence (Shot Clock Turns off Under 30 Seconds)
trigger_condition: The game clock drops under 30 seconds at the end of the 1st Half, 2nd Half, or Overtime.
editor_action: When less than 30 seconds remain in a half, the 30-second shot timer turns off because the main game clock has less time than the shot timer. Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide locked for the final play, pre-arm the overhead backboard camera to verify if a buzzer-beater left the player's fingertips before the red backboard light flashed, and transition to halftime/final stats after the horn.
timing_constraint: Continuous wide hold for the final possession, followed by buzzer celebration/review and end-of-period summary (example: final 18s to 30s of half).
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Mid-Replay Preemption: Speed-Ramp Finish vs. Immediate Hard-Cut Bailout
trigger_condition: A slow-motion replay is still playing when the referee prepares to hand the ball to the free-throw shooter or throw-in passer.
editor_action: If the replay is less than 1 second away from showing the ball go through the hoop and the live ball is not yet in play, briefly speed up the replay (1.5x speed-ramp) so viewers see the finish before cutting back to CAM-1 (Main Wide). If the live ball is already in the player's hands ready to pass or shoot, cut immediately to CAM-1 (Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Speed-ramp if <1.0s to highlight climax before throw-in; hard-cut immediately (<0.2s) if live ball is already active.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Ambiguous Whistle Hold (Waiting for Referee Hand Signal Before Committing)
trigger_condition: A whistle blows during a crowded play near the basket, and for the first 1 to 2 seconds it is not yet clear whether the referee called a defensive foul, an offensive charge, a travel, a jump ball, or out-of-bounds.
editor_action: Do not guess the call or flash a foul graphic prematurely. Hold a medium-wide CAM-1 (Main Wide) or CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) view that keeps both the players and the referee in frame until the referee makes their official hand signal, then trigger the matching replay and scoreboard explanation.
timing_constraint: Hold medium-wide framing for the 1.0s to 2.0s whistle-to-signal verification window before triggering call-specific graphics.
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: Shot-Clock Under 5 Seconds Overrides All Non-Live Requests
trigger_condition: The 30-second shot clock drops to 5 seconds or less during a live possession while the Graphics or Audio agent requests a stat card or cutaway. (Visual cue: Shot clock glowing amber/red at :05 and counting down; Audio cue: Rising crowd murmur as the offense must force up a shot.)
editor_action: Lock the video feed on CAM-1 (Main Wide) and suppress all new graphic overlays when the shot clock is at 5 seconds or below, because a shot attempt, block, or shot-clock violation is guaranteed to happen within seconds (example: hard lock on CAM-1 (Main Wide) for shot clock <= 5s). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Queue any pending graphic card to appear on the subsequent stoppage or after the defensive rebound is secured.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Player Injury on Floor Preempts Celebration & Replay
trigger_condition: A player scores a basket or commits a turnover, but another player remains down on the hardwood holding their ankle or knee. (Visual cue: Nine players transition downcourt while one player lies motionless or limping on the floor; Audio cue: Crowd hush and announcer noticing a player is slow to get up.)
editor_action: Once play stops for the injury, immediately cancel celebratory bench cuts, upbeat music stingers, and promotional graphics, shifting to a respectful medium shot while medical staff attend to the player (example: P1 Safety/Injury override suppresses P4/P5 entertainment elements). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Respectful Medium Shot.
timing_constraint: Target window: P1 Safety/Injury override suppresses P4/P5 entertainment elements. Do not loop gruesome slow-motion replays of a severe joint injury.

title: Clutch Final-Minute Scorebug Lock vs. Sponsor Bugs
trigger_condition: The game enters the final 60 seconds of the second half or overtime with a margin of 6 points or less, and a scheduled sponsor logo or trivia graphic is queued. (Visual cue: Game clock under 1:00 in a one- or two-possession game; Audio cue: High-tension clutch play-by-play.)
editor_action: Suppress all non-essential sponsor bugs, trivia cards, and upcoming-game promos during the final 60 seconds of a close game so 100% of graphic attention remains on the score, clock, shot clock, timeouts remaining, and team foul bonus (example: P1 Clutch Situational HUD locks out P5 promotional graphics). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Reschedule any deferred promotional read to an earlier timeout or post-game wrap-up (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)
plain_english_tip: Bonus rule: At 7+ team fouls in a half, opponents shoot 1-and-1 free throws; at 10+ fouls (Double Bonus), they get 2 automatic free throws.

title: Phantom Whistle from Crowd vs. Official Referee Stoppage
trigger_condition: A high-pitched whistle-like noise comes from the crowd, causing one or two players to hesitate while others keep playing. (Visual cue: Referees are NOT raising their arms or signaling a dead ball, and the game clock continues to run; Audio cue: Faint whistle sound without referee arm signal or clock stop.)
editor_action: Never cut away from CAM-1 (Main Wide) on an audio whistle cue alone unless corroborated by either the official game clock stopping or a referee visibly raising their hand to signal a dead ball (example: require audio whistle + clock stop/referee signal before dead-ball cuts). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: require audio whistle + clock stop/referee signal before dead-ball cuts. Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) locked whenever the game clock is actively counting down.

title: Stopping The Game Clock on a Referee's Whistle (Dead-Ball Coordination)
trigger_condition: A referee blows the whistle to stop play (because of a foul, a ball going out of bounds, or a rule violation) outside the final two minutes of a close game.
editor_action: Coordinate all four broadcast roles during the pause: first show a quick close-up of the player involved, then roll a slow-motion replay if there was physical contact near the basket, and finally display an on-screen stat banner before live play starts again.
timing_constraint: Finish the entire sequence while the game clock is stopped and return to the wide full-court camera before the referee hands the ball back to a player (example: 9s foul pause).

title: Fast-Break Steal Preempts Active Lower-Third Stat Card
trigger_condition: While a large player biography or statistical comparison card is displayed on the lower third of the screen during a calm half-court set, a defender pokes the ball loose and starts a fast break. (Visual cue: Sudden turnover and sprint in the opposite direction; Audio cue: Announcer shouts 'Stolen!'.)
editor_action: Instantly animate the lower-third stat card off the screen within ~0.3 seconds when a live-ball steal occurs so the full court is unobstructed for the fast-break sprint (example: P1 Live Transition overrides P5 Graphic Card). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Never leave a multi-line graphic blocking the bottom of the screen during a full-court sprint (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Buzzer-Beater Forensic Review Overrides End-Of-Half Bump
trigger_condition: A player releases a shot right as the half or game horn sounds, and the ball goes in, requiring officials to review whether it beat the clock. (Visual cue: Red backboard LEDs lit while officials gather at the scorer's table; Audio cue: Horn and crowd roar followed by referee whistle for review.)
editor_action: Hold off the end-of-half commercial break until the Replay Agent displays the definitive slow-motion angle showing the player's fingertips and the 0.0 backboard light, and the referee announces whether the basket counts (example: P2 Score Verification overrides P3 Halftime Break). Recommended framing: Synchronized Clock + Release Replay (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Update the scorebug points only after the referee gives the final confirmed signal.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Quick Inbound After Made Basket Cancels Replay Queue
trigger_condition: A player hits a spectacular dunk, queuing a high-priority post-score hero cut or quick look-in, but the opposing point guard immediately grabs the ball out of the net and sprints upcourt. (Visual cue: Inbound pass completed within 1.0 second of the ball passing through the net; Audio cue: Announcer shifts tone from celebrating the dunk to calling the fast break the other way.)
editor_action: Abort or immediately terminate the post-dunk hero close-up if the opposing team pushes the ball across the backcourt at sprint speed, saving the dunk celebration and replay for the next dead-ball whistle (example: P1 Live Fast-Break overrides P3 Post-Score Hero Cut). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Tag the dunk timestamp in the Replay Agent's memory buffer so it is guaranteed to air at the next timeout (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Final Buzzer Winner Reaction vs. Final Scoreboard Graphic Priority
trigger_condition: The game ends on a thrilling final play as the second-half horn sounds at 0.0s. (Visual cue: Winning team celebrating on the floor while the losing team walks off; Audio cue: Final horn and lead announcer's sign-off call.)
editor_action: Keep the video focused full-screen on the emotional player reactions and handshakes for the first 15 to 20 seconds after the horn while showing the 'FINAL' score in the compact corner scorebug, delaying full-screen box-score tables until the initial celebration peaks (example: ~18s pure emotion window before full-screen stat tables). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) + Compact Final Scorebug.
timing_constraint: Ensure the word 'FINAL' is locked on the scorebug only after confirming no buzzer-beater review is needed.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Halftime Multi-Highlight Montage & Storyline Bridge
trigger_condition: The first-half buzzer sounds (0.0s), sending the teams to the locker rooms for halftime. (Visual cue: Players and coaches walking through the arena tunnel toward the locker rooms; Audio cue: Halftime horn and announcer summarizing the first-half score.)
editor_action: Show the leading scorer or coach walking toward the locker-room tunnel (or a quick courtside interview), followed by a 3-clip montage of the biggest plays of the first half and a full-screen halftime stat comparison before handing off to the halftime studio show (example: ~15-20s halftime bridge sequence). Recommended framing: Tunnel Walk (CAM-2, Baseline Low) -> 3-Clip First-Half Montage.
timing_constraint: Target window: ~15-20s halftime bridge sequence. Lock 'HALFTIME' on the scorebug once any final first-half buzzer shot is confirmed.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Short 30-Second / Clutch Timeout Stay-In-Arena Rule
trigger_condition: A coach calls a 30-second timeout (or a timeout inside the final 2 minutes of a close second half) where the broadcast stays live in the arena instead of going to commercials. (Visual cue: Both teams huddling around their coaches while the arena buzzes; Audio cue: Analysts breaking down the tactical chess match for the upcoming play.)
editor_action: Stay inside the arena rather than cutting to commercials during 30-second or final-minute clutch timeouts, cycling between both coaching huddles, a replay of the last pivotal play, and the foul/timeout situation on the scorebug (example: 30-60s in-arena clutch timeout coverage). Recommended framing: Bench Huddle (CAM-4, Coach & Bench) -> Tactical Replay -> CAM-1 (Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: 30-60s in-arena clutch timeout coverage. Return to CAM-1 (Main Wide) as soon as the timeout horn sounds so viewers see the exact alignment of the drawn-up play.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Injury Timeout Respectful Bumper Transition
trigger_condition: Play is stopped for an extended period while athletic trainers evaluate an injured player on the court, and the broadcast takes an injury commercial break. (Visual cue: Teammates kneeling or standing quietly around the injured player; Audio cue: Somber, respectful commentary tone.)
editor_action: Transition to commercial break without upbeat celebratory music or flashy dunk replays, using a calm ambient arena shot and quiet bumper card while medical staff do their work (example: mute upbeat music stinger on injury breaks). Recommended framing: Wide Arena / Respectful Medium -> Quiet Bumper to Break.
timing_constraint: Upon returning from the break, immediately provide a sideline reporter update on the injured player's status (Complete transition >= 3.0s before referee hands ball to inbounder.)
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Motion-Blur / Out-Of-Focus Iso Camera Instant Bailout
trigger_condition: The director cuts to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) or CAM-2 (Baseline Low), and the incoming camera feed is noticeably out of focus or whip-panning to find the subject. (Visual cue: Blurry image or rapid unintentional camera shake on the active program feed; Audio cue: Any game audio.)
editor_action: If an active close-up camera loses focus or suffers a violent pan for more than half a second, bail out immediately back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) rather than waiting on air for the camera operator to hunt for focus (example: < 0.5s bailout to CAM-1 (Main Wide) on focus loss). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Pre-check focus sharpness on the preview bus before cutting any tight camera to air.

title: Rapid Back-To-Back Turnovers Stabilization Rule
trigger_condition: Team A steals the ball, then immediately loses it back to Team B within 2 seconds in a chaotic midcourt scramble. (Visual cue: Loose ball ping-ponging between multiple diving and lunging players near midcourt; Audio cue: Rapid-fire play-by-play commentary ('Stolen! Lost it! Taken back!').)
editor_action: When possession changes twice within 3 seconds, freeze all camera-switching and graphic-triggering logic and keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) zoomed comfortably wide around midcourt until one team clearly establishes control of the basketball (example: suppress all cuts and graphics during chaotic multi-turnover scrambles). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Reset the 30-second shot clock on the scorebug in sync with the official arena reset (Trigger safe-harbor fallback to CAM-1 Wide within < 0.5s of confidence drop.)
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Halftime Intermission Outbound & Second-Half Team Foul Reset
trigger_condition: The horn sounds to end the 1st Half (00:00 1ST) and players walk toward the locker rooms.
editor_action: Follow the leading scorer and both head coaches walking off the floor on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-4, display the Full-Screen Halftime Team Comparison (shooting %, rebounds, turnovers, and top scorers), and reset both teams' foul counts to 0 in the scoreboard before the 2nd Half begins.
timing_constraint: Run halftime walk-off and full-screen stat summary over the 10s to 15s post-horn window; reset team fouls to 0 for 2nd Half.
plain_english_tip: Bonus rule: At 7+ team fouls in a half, opponents shoot 1-and-1 free throws; at 10+ fouls (Double Bonus), they get 2 automatic free throws.

title: Pre-Tip-Off Cold Open: Starting Lineups & Plain-English 'Keys to The Game'
trigger_condition: The final 60 seconds before the opening jump ball at center court (20:00 1ST).
editor_action: Introduce the matchup for viewers tuning in: show both head coaches on CAM-4, display the 5-player Starting Lineup graphics for the Away and Home teams, show a simple 2-bullet 'Keys to the Game' card explaining what each team needs to do to win, and settle on CAM-1 (Main Wide) at least 5 seconds before the opening jump ball.
timing_constraint: Complete Starting Lineup and Keys to the Game graphics at least 5.0s before the opening tip-off.

title: Four-Agent Relay Choreography on 'And-One' Basket-Plus-Foul Plays
trigger_condition: A player makes a basket while being fouled, creating a 15-to-20 second stoppage where Director, Replay, and Graphics all have high-value outputs.
editor_action: Instead of letting agents talk over each other, run a clean 4-step relay: Step 1: Director cuts to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) for the scorer's celebration -> Step 2: Replay rolls slow-motion contact and basket with the scoreboard hidden -> Step 3: Director cuts back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) for the free-throw line-up with the scoreboard restored -> Step 4: Graphics displays the shooter's free-throw % banner.
timing_constraint: Sequence Step 1 Reaction (example: 2.5s) -> Step 2 Slow-Mo Replay (example: 5.0s) -> Step 3 CAM-1 Setup -> Step 4 FT Stat Banner (example: 5.0s).
plain_english_tip: And-One: If a player scores while being fouled, the basket counts and they earn 1 bonus free throw.

title: Human Showmaker Manual Override Grace Period ('Hands-Off' Cooldown)
trigger_condition: The human Showmaker manually clicks a camera button in the control room to override the AI agent's current camera selection.
editor_action: When a human operator manually chooses a camera, pause automated AI camera switching for a brief grace period so the AI does not immediately fight the human operator and switch back a half-second later, unless an emergency fast break or court-safety takeover requires CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide.
timing_constraint: Hold a manual override grace period after any human camera take (example: 4.5s to 6.0s cooldown before resuming automated cuts).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Going-To-Commercial-Break 3-Step Outbound Tease Sequence
trigger_condition: A scheduled TV media timeout or full team timeout triggers an upcoming commercial break.
editor_action: Never cut abruptly from a live court whistle straight to commercials. Run a smooth 3-step transition into the break: Step 1: Show the players walking to their bench huddle on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) -> Step 2: Roll the best slow-motion highlight from the last few minutes -> Step 3: Show the full-screen score bumper card with theme music as the broadcast goes to break.
timing_constraint: Run the 3-step outbound bumper sequence over the 6s to 8s window leading into the commercial splice.

title: Returning-From-Commercial-Break 10-Second Viewer Re-Orientation
trigger_condition: The broadcast returns from a commercial break back to the live arena just before play restarts.
editor_action: Welcome viewers back by opening on a wide arena or bench huddle view (CAM-1 (Main Wide) or CAM-4 (Coach & Bench)), restoring the scoreboard immediately, and if any free throws, technical fouls, or official video reviews happened during the break, flashing a plain-English 'What Happened During the Break' note before the throw-in.
timing_constraint: Complete re-orientation and transition to CAM-1 Wide at least 3.0s before the referee hands the ball to the inbounder.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Comeback Trail Tracker (Cutting a Double-Digit Lead Under 5 Points)
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a team that trailed by 10+ points trims the deficit to 5 points or fewer.
editor_action: Pair a 'Largest Lead vs. Current Margin' graphic with a 2-clip comeback replay package and a CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) shot of the opposing coach calling timeout.
timing_constraint: Trigger on the basket or timeout that cuts a 10+ point deficit to <= 5 points (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Explaining 'One-And-One' (7 to 9 Team Fouls) vs. Two-Shot Double Bonus
trigger_condition: A non-shooting foul is called when the defense has 7, 8, or 9 team fouls in the half ('One-and-One' Bonus).
editor_action: Trigger a plain-English scoreboard note ('1-and-1 Bonus: Make 1st Free Throw to Earn 2nd Shot') and alert the Director Agent to stay ready on CAM-1 (Main Wide) for a live rebound on the 1st free throw.
timing_constraint: Display 1-and-1 explanation before Shot 1 and arm CAM-1 rebound lock on Shot 1 release.
plain_english_tip: Bonus rule: At 7+ team fouls in a half, opponents shoot 1-and-1 free throws; at 10+ fouls (Double Bonus), they get 2 automatic free throws.

title: Coach's Challenge / Official Video Review Trigger & Outcome
trigger_condition: A head coach requests an official video review (or referees initiate a monitor check in the final 2 minutes) on out-of-bounds touch, goaltending, or shot-clock expiry.
editor_action: Immediately switch into Official Review Mode: show the referees at the scorer's table on CAM-4, loop the two sharpest replay angles in synchronized slow motion, and display a 'Call Under Review' banner followed by 'Call Stands / Call Overturned'.
timing_constraint: Run throughout the 30s to 90s monitor review until the referee announces the decision.
plain_english_tip: Goaltending: Defenders cannot swat a shot once it is on its downward arc toward the hoop; doing so awards automatic points.

title: Timeout Remaining Inventory Alert (0 or 1 Timeout Left in Crunch Time)
trigger_condition: A team uses its second-to-last or final timeout with more than 1 minute remaining in a close game.
editor_action: Pulse the team's timeout indicator bars on the Scorebug and flash '1 Timeout Remaining' or '0 Timeouts Remaining' so viewers know whether the team can stop the clock on its final possession.
timing_constraint: Flash for 5.0s coming out of the timeout when remaining timeouts <= 1.

title: Fouling up 3 Points in The Final 10 Seconds (Preventing a Tying 3-Pointer)
trigger_condition: The leading team is ahead by 3 points in the final 10 seconds and intentionally fouls the ball-handler before they can attempt a 3-point shot.
editor_action: Flash a tactical explanation banner ('Strategic Foul Up 3: Force 2 Free Throws Instead of a Tying 3-Pointer') as the player walks to the free-throw line.
timing_constraint: Display during the free-throw walk-up in the final 10.0s when margin == 3.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Blood Rule / Uniform Number Swap Sideline Stoppage
trigger_condition: Referees stop play because a player has a small cut/bleed or torn jersey and must either be bandaged within 20 seconds or subbed out.
editor_action: Keep the camera respectful (medium CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) on the coach/bench rather than a graphic close-up of blood) and flash 'Equipment / Medical Timeout Stoppage' on the scoreboard.
timing_constraint: Hold medium CAM-4 or replay package until the substitution or bandage is complete.

title: First-Possession-After-Halftime Set Play Tracking
trigger_condition: The opening possession of the 2nd Half (20:00 2ND) right after halftime intermission.
editor_action: Lock CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide on the opening possession of the 2nd Half while the Graphics Agent queues a 'Halftime Adjustments' note summarizing what the trailing team's coach emphasized.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 Wide for the first 20s of the 2nd Half.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Act 2 (Middle of The Game): Riding Momentum Swings and Back-And-Forth Runs
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Mid-1st Half through Mid-2nd Half): The core body of the game where teams trade baskets, adjust strategies, and go on scoring streaks.
editor_action: Shift into an energetic storytelling rhythm: pair made baskets with quick player close-ups, check in on the coaches on the sideline when a team goes on a scoring streak, and package the best 2 or 3 plays into mini-highlight reels at each commercial break so a viewer tuning in mid-game immediately understands the story so far.
timing_constraint: Balanced mid-game switching pace combining live wide play with dead-ball replays and stat banners (example: ~11 to 13 cuts per minute during active runs) (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Building The Story of an Unanswered 'Scoring Run' (Momentum Shift)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Multi-Possession Run): One team scores 6, 8, or 10+ points in a row while holding the other team scoreless.
editor_action: Build excitement across consecutive trips down the court: pair each made basket with a close-up of the cheering scorers and a reaction shot of the opposing coach looking concerned on the sideline, then display a 'Scoring Run' banner (such as '8-0 Run over the last 2:00') and roll a multi-clip highlight reel when a timeout is finally called.
timing_constraint: Escalate player-to-coach reaction cuts across consecutive baskets culminating in the timeout highlight reel (example: 3-possession buildup into timeout) (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Explaining College Basketball's Four Scheduled TV Timeouts Each Half (Under-16/12/8/4)
trigger_condition: The first dead-ball whistle after the game clock crosses under 16:00, 12:00, 8:00, or 4:00 in either half.
editor_action: In college basketball, automatic television timeouts happen at the first whistle under the 16-, 12-, 8-, and 4-minute marks of each half. Automatically prepare the commercial-break sequence as the clock crosses those marks so the moment the whistle blows, the broadcast smoothly rolls player reactions, a multi-play highlight reel, and the score bumper.
timing_constraint: Pre-arm the highlight reel as the clock crosses 16:00, 12:00, 8:00, or 4:00 and execute the break sequence on the whistle (example: 14s media timeout package).

title: When a Player Commits Their 5th Personal Foul and Is Disqualified ('Fouling Out')
trigger_condition: A player commits their 5th personal foul of the game and must leave the court for the remainder of the broadcast.
editor_action: Because college players are disqualified after 5 personal fouls, treat a key player 'fouling out' as a major story moment: roll a slow-motion replay of the 5th foul, switch to CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) to follow the player walking off to their coach and bench, and display their full-game stats alongside the replacement player checking in.
timing_constraint: Use the extended substitution time allowed for a disqualified player to show the replay, walk-off, and final stat line (example: 12s to 18s foul-out sequence).
plain_english_tip: Foul Limit: In college basketball, any player who commits 5 personal fouls is disqualified for the rest of the game.

title: Returning from a Timeout: Showing The Coach's Drawn-Up Play Setup
trigger_condition: The buzzer sounds to end a 30-second or full timeout, and both teams walk back onto the court.
editor_action: Cut back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) at least 3 seconds before the referee hands the ball to the inbounder so viewers can see how the 5 offensive players line up for the special play their coach just drew up on the whiteboard during the timeout.
timing_constraint: Establish wide full-court framing 3.0s before the post-timeout throw-in begins.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Sharp Referee Whistle Audio Trigger (Pre-Visual Dead-Ball Detection)
trigger_condition: Court microphones detect a sharp referee whistle blast before the scoreboard game clock visually stops or before players stop running.
editor_action: Use the acoustic whistle spike as an early dead-ball warning (~0.5s before visual clock stop) so the Replay Agent immediately marks the preceding 6-second highlight clip and the Graphics Agent pre-checks queued Font 1 banners while the Director holds CAM-1 (Main Wide) to see the referee's signal.
timing_constraint: Trigger tentative dead-ball prep within a sub-second beat of the acoustic whistle spike (example: 0.4s lead time before scoreboard clock stops).

title: Queued Graphic 'Time-To-Live' (TTL) Expiration When The Game Situation Changes
trigger_condition: A situational graphic (such as '10-0 Scoring Run' or 'Cold Shooting Streak: 0 of 7') is waiting in the preview queue for a whistle, but live play continues.
editor_action: Give every queued momentum graphic a 1-possession expiration timer (Time-To-Live). If the other team scores to end the run or the cold shooter makes a basket before a whistle happens, automatically cancel and delete the queued graphic so outdated information never airs two minutes later.
timing_constraint: Expire and purge queued momentum graphics after 1 possession (~30s to 45s) or immediately if the underlying stat is invalidated.

title: Cold Shooting Drought & Scoring Dry-Spell Tracker
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a team goes scoreless for more than 3 minutes of game clock or misses 6+ consecutive field goals.
editor_action: Show the frustrated coach on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) alongside a Scorebug drought badge ('No Field Goals in Last 3:30') so viewers feel the mounting pressure to score.
timing_constraint: Activate drought tracker once a scoreless stretch exceeds 3:00 of game clock (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Cylinder / Restricted-Arc Block vs. Charge Rule Explainer
trigger_condition: A collision under the basket results in a blocking foul because the defender's heel was touching the curved restricted arc painted under the hoop.
editor_action: Cue the Replay Agent to show the overhead CAM-5 (Above-Rim) angle looking straight down at the curved arc line under the basket, and display a note ('Restricted Arc: Defender Inside Arc Cannot Draw a Charge').
timing_constraint: Coordinate CAM-5 arc replay + plain-English note during free-throw walk-up (example: 4.5s).
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: Hook-And-Hold / Flagrant Contact Monitor Check
trigger_condition: Referees go to the courtside monitor to check whether an elbow to the face or a rebound 'hook-and-hold' rises to a Flagrant 1 or Flagrant 2 foul.
editor_action: Cue a zoomed-in slow-motion replay of the upper-body contact and display a plain-English explainer comparing Common Foul vs. Flagrant 1 (2 free throws + keep the ball).
timing_constraint: Loop contact angle + penalty explainer during the monitor review window (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Foul-To-Give Strategy (Fouling When Only at 4 or 5 Team Fouls Late)
trigger_condition: In the final minute of a close game, a defense has fewer than 6 team fouls and intentionally fouls on the perimeter to take 2-3 seconds off the game clock without giving up free throws.
editor_action: Flash 'Foul to Give: 5th Team Foul (No Free Throws Yet)' on the scoreboard so casual viewers understand why the defense fouled on purpose and why the offense is throwing the ball in from the sideline instead of shooting free throws.
timing_constraint: Display during the 3.0s side-out setup after a late-game non-bonus foul.
plain_english_tip: Bonus rule: At 7+ team fouls in a half, opponents shoot 1-and-1 free throws; at 10+ fouls (Double Bonus), they get 2 automatic free throws.

title: Clear-Path / Transition Take Foul Explanation (2 Free Throws + Keep The Ball)
trigger_condition: A defender grabs a fast-break player from behind with no defender between them and the basket.
editor_action: Coordinate a slow-motion CAM-1 (Main Wide) replay showing the open court ahead of the runner and display 'Transition Clear-Path Foul: 2 Free Throws + Team Keeps Possession'.
timing_constraint: Run replay + penalty explanation during the dead-ball review/free-throw walk-up (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Going to Commercial Break or Team Timeout (Highlight Reel Sequence)
trigger_condition: A scheduled television commercial break ('media timeout') or a coach calling a timeout to stop the other team's momentum.
editor_action: Guide viewers into the break in three clear steps: (1) show the scoring player celebrating and the coaches gathering their teams on the sideline, (2) play two or three of the most exciting highlights from the recent stretch, and (3) show the full-screen score and matchup graphic.
timing_constraint: Fit the player reactions, highlight clips, and score graphic smoothly into the transition window before commercials begin (example: 14s to 15s break sequence).

title: Coordinating Official Referee Video Reviews at The Scorer's Table
trigger_condition: Referees stop the game and walk to the courtside monitor to check who touched the ball last, whether a foul was unsportsmanlike ('flagrant'), or how much time should be on the clock.
editor_action: Switch the control room into Official Review Mode: put up an 'Official Review' note explaining in plain words what the referees are checking, hide the bottom scoreboard so zoomed-in slow-motion replays fill the screen cleanly, and cut back to the live referee the instant they step away from the monitor to give the verdict.
timing_constraint: Hold synchronized slow-motion review loops for the duration of the monitor check and return to live view on referee step-away (example: 15s to 20s review window).
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Going to Overtime When The Score Is Tied at The End of Regulation (5-Minute Extra Period)
trigger_condition: The score is tied when the 2nd Half clock hits 00:00.0.
editor_action: Basketball games cannot end in a tie; each overtime period adds 5 extra minutes starting with a new center-court jump ball. Show the dramatic reactions of both benches after the final regulation shot misses, display an 'Overtime (5:00 Extra Period)' graphic showing reset team timeouts, and return to CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide for the overtime tip-off.
timing_constraint: Bridge the end-of-regulation horn to the 5:00 overtime tip-off with bench reactions, clutch replay, and overtime rules reset (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Underdog Upset Watch & Tournament Survival Tension
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Second-Half Upset or Elimination Arc): An unranked or underdog team leads or stays tied with a heavily favored powerhouse in the second half, or a tournament elimination game enters its final 10 minutes.
editor_action: Elevate the emotional stakes across the second half: increase dead-ball check-ins on both coaches and benches (CAM-4, Coach & Bench), capture the crowd's rising anticipation after every underdog basket, and surface tournament bracket or season-series context during timeouts so viewers feel the weight of a potential upset.
timing_constraint: Increase bench/crowd reaction frequency during second-half dead balls when an upset or elimination is on the line (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Handling Technical Fouls & Unsportsmanlike ('Flagrant') Fouls
trigger_condition: A referee blows the whistle and forms a 'T' or an 'X' with their arms for a technical foul (unsportsmanlike arguing/taunting) or a flagrant foul (excessive physical contact).
editor_action: Because a technical or flagrant foul gives the other team two free throws PLUS possession of the ball afterward, coordinate a clear explanation: show the referee's signal on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-4, roll a slow-motion replay if physical contact was involved, and display a scoreboard banner explaining that the team gets free throws and keeps the ball.
timing_constraint: Coordinate referee signal, replay check, and plain-English penalty banner during the stoppage (example: 12s to 20s sequence).
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Coach's Challenge / Review Request Preempts Standard Highlight Replay
trigger_condition: After an out-of-bounds or basket-interference whistle, the Replay Agent queues a highlight of the previous basket, but the head coach signals for an NCAA Coach's Challenge / Official Monitor Review. (Visual cue: Head coach signaling toward the officials to request a video monitor challenge; Audio cue: Whistle and announcer exclaiming 'He is going to challenge the call!'.)
editor_action: Cancel the unrelated previous-basket highlight replay and immediately switch priority to showing the coach requesting the review, followed by the forensic multi-angle replay of the challenged out-of-bounds or goaltending call within 2.0 seconds (example: P2 Official Review Challenge preempts P4 routine highlight). Recommended framing: Bench Reaction (CAM-4, Coach & Bench) -> Forensic Review Replay.
timing_constraint: Display an 'OFFICIAL REVIEW / CHALLENGE' banner on the scorebug until the referee announces the ruling.
plain_english_tip: Goaltending: Defenders cannot swat a shot once it is on its downward arc toward the hoop; doing so awards automatic points.

title: Sideline Reporter Live Audio vs. Immediate Play Resume Split-Screen
trigger_condition: The sideline reporter is halfway through a crucial 15-second injury or coach update when the referee hands the ball to the inbounder to resume live play. (Visual cue: Players stepping onto the court while the reporter is still speaking on camera; Audio cue: Sideline reporter speaking mid-sentence.)
editor_action: Resolve the conflict between P1 Live Action and P3 Sideline Report by cutting the video immediately back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) (or a small side box for the reporter) while keeping the reporter's microphone live for the remaining few seconds until they finish their thought (example: video prioritizes P1 court; audio finishes P3 report for <= 6s). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) with Reporter Audio / Picture-in-Picture.
timing_constraint: If a dramatic basket or foul occurs during those 6 seconds, the play-by-play announcer may interrupt and take back audio priority.

title: First-Shot vs. Second-Shot Free-Throw Arbitration Window
trigger_condition: During a two-shot free-throw trip, both the Replay Agent (wanting to show the foul) and the Graphics Agent (wanting to show shooter stats) request the gap after the first free throw. (Visual cue: Shooter completes the first free throw and waits for the referee to bounce the ball back for the second attempt (~7-second window); Audio cue: Analyst commenting on the foul call.)
editor_action: If the foul call was controversial or a highlight play, grant the 5-second window between free throws to the Replay Agent; if it was a routine foul, grant the window to the Director + Graphics Agent for a tight shot of the shooter with their free-throw stat pill (example: mutual exclusion between full-screen replay and shooter stat card between Shot 1 and Shot 2). Recommended framing: Replay after Shot 1 (if controversial) OR Hero Iso + Stat Card.
timing_constraint: Whichever agent wins the window must yield back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) at least 1 second before the second free throw is released.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Mandatory Under-16 / 12 / 8 / 4 Media Timeout Anticipation
trigger_condition: The half clock ticks below 16:00, 12:00, 8:00, or 4:00 while play is still continuous, meaning the very next whistle will automatically trigger a mandatory NCAA television commercial timeout. (Visual cue: Half clock crossing below 16:00, 12:00, 8:00, or 4:00 with no media timeout yet taken in that segment; Audio cue: Play-by-play announcer notes that the next whistle will bring a media timeout.)
editor_action: Pre-stage the best highlight clip of the current 4-minute segment and prepare the outgoing score bumper as soon as the clock passes the mandatory media-timeout mark so the transition to commercials is seamless on the next whistle (example: pre-queue top highlight when clock crosses 16:00, 12:00, 8:00, or 4:00). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Hero Bump (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Wait for the actual dead-ball whistle (foul, out-of-bounds, or timeout call) before rolling the bumper.

title: Mid-Half Under-12 & Under-8 Media Break Bumper Sequence
trigger_condition: A whistle stops play below the 12:00 or 8:00 mark of a half, triggering a full NCAA media timeout break. (Visual cue: Players walking back to their benches as the red media-timeout hat steps onto the court; Audio cue: Whistle and announcer stating the score and time remaining heading to break.)
editor_action: Capture the emotion of the player who made the signature play of the 4-minute segment, roll one slow-motion highlight over the outgoing music bed, and display the current score and clock bumper heading to commercial (example: ~8-10s media-break bumper sequence). Recommended framing: Hero Reaction (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Best Play of Segment Replay -> Score Bumper.
timing_constraint: Verify whether free throws will be shot before or after the commercial break and inform viewers clearly.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Overtime Period Transition & Reset Structure
trigger_condition: The second half ends with both teams tied in score, sending the game into a 5-minute Overtime period. (Visual cue: Scoreboard showing a tied score at 0.0s at the end of regulation as players catch their breath; Audio cue: Announcer exclaims 'We are headed to overtime!'.)
editor_action: Replay the final regulation shot from two definitive angles, show both exhausted stars on their benches, reset the timeout counts on the scorebug for the 5-minute overtime period, and frame the center circle for the overtime jump ball (example: full overtime situational reset before tip). Recommended framing: Hero / Bench Reactions -> Replay of Game-Tying / Missed Final Shot -> Center Circle (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Never cut away to a long commercial break during the short 1-minute intermission before overtime.

title: Pre-Game Starting Lineups & Keys to The Game Sequence
trigger_condition: The final 90 seconds before the opening tip-off as starters shed their warmups. (Visual cue: Starters huddling with teammates and walking to center court; Audio cue: Commentators outlining the 2 or 3 main strategic keys for each team.)
editor_action: Present Away Starting 5, Home Starting 5, and a concise 3-bullet 'Keys to the Game' graphic in plain English (e.g., 'Protect the Paint', 'Limit Turnovers', 'Slow Down #X') so a new viewer understands what both teams are trying to accomplish tonight (example: ~45s pre-tip primer). Recommended framing: Star Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) + Starting 5 Graphic -> CAM-1 (Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Finish all pre-game graphics at least 3 seconds before the opening jump ball.

title: Referee Steps Across Baseline Camera Lens Fallback
trigger_condition: While showing a post-basket reaction on CAM-2 (Baseline Low), a referee or another player walks directly in front of the lens, filling the screen with their back. (Visual cue: Sudden full-frame occlusion of the target player by a passing body; Audio cue: Post-play commentary.)
editor_action: Cut away to CAM-1 (Main Wide) or an unobstructed sideline iso camera within ~0.4 seconds whenever a foreground body blocks more than half of the active close-up frame (example: instant cut on > 50% subject occlusion). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide) or Secondary Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Avoid cutting back to the obstructed baseline camera until the referee has moved away.

title: Jersey-Number Attribution Uncertainty Guardrail
trigger_condition: A foul is called in a crowded paint scramble where #23 and #32 are standing next to each other, and the official scorer has not yet posted who committed the foul. (Visual cue: Multiple defenders in the paint looking at the referee; Audio cue: Commentator says 'Foul inside, let's see who they get it on.'.)
editor_action: Hold off on displaying a specific player's personal-foul graphic until the referee reports the jersey number to the scorer's table and the official play-by-play feed confirms the player ID (example: wait ~1.5-2.0s for official scorer confirmation before firing foul pill). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: wait ~1.5-2.0s for official scorer confirmation before firing foul pill. Never guess and flash a '4th Foul' warning on the wrong player when jersey numbers are ambiguous.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Audio Mic Dropout / Static Automatic Failover
trigger_condition: A sideline reporter's wireless microphone or a courtside shotgun mic experiences RF static, popping, or signal dropout. (Visual cue: Sideline reporter speaking on camera while audio crackles or drops out; Audio cue: RF static burst or complete silence on the active mic channel.)
editor_action: Automatically mute a crackling or silent wireless microphone within 1 second and hand audio back to the booth play-by-play announcer while cutting video back to the court (CAM-1, Main Wide) so the broadcast never airs sustained static or dead silence (example: < 1.0s audio failover to booth commentary). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: < 1.0s audio failover to booth commentary. Play-by-play announcer smoothly summarizes the sideline update once back on air.

title: Baseline Camera Operator Bump / Collision Recovery
trigger_condition: A player diving for a loose ball or momentum-carrying layup crashes into the baseline camera area where CAM-2 (Baseline Low) is positioned. (Visual cue: Player sliding into the padded stanchion or baseline photographers; Audio cue: Crowd gasp and whistle.)
editor_action: If a player collides near the baseline camera position, immediately view the scene from CAM-1 (Main Wide) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) rather than cutting to the jarred baseline camera (CAM-2, Baseline Low), ensuring a stable image and checking that both the player and camera crew are okay (example: suppress CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) selection for ~5s after baseline collision). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) or Opposite Angle (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Resume using CAM-2 (Baseline Low) only after its image is stable and re-framed.

title: Record-Breaking Milestone Overrides Routine Timeout Bump
trigger_condition: A player scores a basket that breaks a career, franchise, or single-game scoring record, and a timeout is immediately called. (Visual cue: Arena scoreboard flashing a milestone graphic while fans give a standing ovation; Audio cue: Lead announcer calling the historic milestone.)
editor_action: Delay the standard commercial break transition by 10 to 15 seconds so the Director and Graphics agents can showcase the player acknowledging the crowd alongside the full milestone stat banner (example: P2 Milestone overrides standard P3 timeout break bump). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) + Milestone Graphic.
timing_constraint: Coordinate with the master break timer so the commercial break still fulfills contractual spot obligations (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)

title: Double-Technical / Altercation Lockout of Automated Tight Cuts
trigger_condition: Two opposing players get chest-to-chest in a heated verbal altercation after a whistle, and teammates/officials rush in to separate them. (Visual cue: Multiple players converging near the paint or sideline after a hard foul; Audio cue: Rapid multiple whistles from officials and rising crowd noise.)
editor_action: Override the Director Agent's impulse to cut to a tight single-face close-up; instead, stay on a medium-wide angle (CAM-1, Main Wide) so the viewer can see the whole separation effort, who is acting as peacemaker, and where the referees are positioned (example: P1 Full-Scene Context overrides P3 Single-Face Iso during altercations). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: P1 Full-Scene Context overrides P3 Single-Face Iso during altercations. Keep court microphones ducked during the confrontation to prevent airing live profanity.

title: Backcourt Violation / 10-Second Count Clock Priority
trigger_condition: Full-court defensive pressure traps the ball-handler in the backcourt as the 30-second shot clock approaches 20 (the NCAA 10-second threshold to cross midcourt). (Visual cue: Ball-handler trapped near the sideline behind the midcourt line with shot clock ticking down 22... 21... 20; Audio cue: Commentator warns 'Watch the 10-second count!'.)
editor_action: Ensure CAM-1 (Main Wide) frames both the trapped ball-handler and the midcourt timeline while highlighting the shot clock on the scorebug so the viewer can see whether the ball crosses midcourt before the shot clock hits 20 (example: P1 Rule-Clock framing priority). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Never cut to a tight close-up of the defender or coach while the 10-second backcourt count is active (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Analyst Telestrator Drawing Lock on Replay Pause
trigger_condition: During a timeout replay, the color analyst uses the telestrator pen to draw arrows or circles on the screen explaining a play. (Visual cue: Yellow or glowing telestrator lines appearing over a paused replay frame; Audio cue: Analyst saying 'Look right here as he sets this screen...'.)
editor_action: Freeze or slow the replay video under the analyst's control and block the Director Agent from cutting away until the analyst finishes their sentence and clears the telestrator drawing, unless live play is already underway on the court (example: P3 Telestrator lock until speech completion or P1 live inbound). Recommended framing: Replay Feed with Telestrator Overlay.
timing_constraint: Target window: P3 Telestrator lock until speech completion or P1 live inbound. Automatically clear all telestrator ink the instant the video cuts back to CAM-1 (Main Wide).

title: Foul Trouble Warning Suppresses Positive Scoring Graphic
trigger_condition: A star scorer who already has 20+ points picks up their 4th personal foul early in the second half, while a pre-built 'Scoring Leader' graphic was queued for them. (Visual cue: Star player looking frustrated as the coach calls a substitute to the scorer's table; Audio cue: Announcer warns 'That is his fourth personal foul, one away from fouling out!'.)
editor_action: Override the queued positive 'Scoring Leader' graphic and instead display the red '4th Personal Foul' alert badge, because foul trouble forcing the star to the bench is the immediate story of the moment (example: P2 Foul-Trouble Alert overrides P4 Scoring Stat Card). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) + Foul Trouble Pill.
timing_constraint: Target window: P2 Foul-Trouble Alert overrides P4 Scoring Stat Card. Save the positive scoring graphic for when the star checks back into the game and scores their next basket.
plain_english_tip: Foul Limit: In college basketball, any player who commits 5 personal fouls is disqualified for the rest of the game.

title: Second-Half Opening Scene-Setter Return
trigger_condition: The broadcast returns from halftime just before the start of the second half. (Visual cue: Players warming up and stepping to midcourt for the second-half inbound; Audio cue: Booth announcers recapping the first-half story and keys to the second half.)
editor_action: Open the second half with a brief look at the first-half statistical leaders and any halftime sideline report on coaching adjustments, then settle onto CAM-1 (Main Wide) before the second-half inbound pass (example: ~10-12s second-half reset before live inbound). Recommended framing: Booth / Courtside -> Star Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Remind viewers which direction each team is now attacking after switching baskets at halftime.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Post-Game Wrap-Up: Final Stats, Star Interview, and Standings Impact
trigger_condition: The game has ended and the initial 20-second handshake celebration on the court concludes. (Visual cue: Players congratulating each other while the sideline reporter prepares for the post-game interview; Audio cue: Commentators summarizing why the winning team prevailed.)
editor_action: Structure the post-game segment in three clear chapters: (1) live courtside interview with the star of the game, (2) a 3-to-4 clip highlight package telling the chronological story of the win, and (3) a final full-screen stat and standings graphic before signing off (example: ~90-120s structured post-game close). Recommended framing: On-Court Interview (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Post-Game Highlight Reel + Final Box Score.
timing_constraint: Target window: ~90-120s structured post-game close. Keep the final score permanently visible throughout the post-game wrap-up.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Official Replay Review In-Arena Hold vs. Commercial Break Decision
trigger_condition: The referees walk to the scorer's table to review a call on the courtside monitor. (Visual cue: Head referee putting on the headset at the replay monitor; Audio cue: Announcer explaining what is under review.)
editor_action: Stay live in the arena during official replay reviews so the Replay Agent and rules analyst can show the viewer every angle of the call and capture the referee's live microphone announcement of the verdict (example: stay in-arena for official reviews unless combined with a mandatory media timeout). Recommended framing: Forensic Multi-Angle Replay + Referee Monitor (CAM-4, Coach & Bench).
timing_constraint: Display the specific review question ('Out of Bounds Review', 'Flagrant Foul Review') clearly on the scorebug (Complete transition >= 3.0s before referee hands ball to inbounder.)

title: Final Broadcast Sign-Off Montage Rhythm
trigger_condition: The broadcast is in its final 30 seconds before handing off to the post-game studio or next program. (Visual cue: Slow-motion cinematic shots of the winning stars, roaring fans, and final scoreboard; Audio cue: Network outro music bed and play-by-play final sign-off.)
editor_action: Close the broadcast with a polished 20-to-30 second montage combining the night's signature dunk/three-pointer, the winning coach's reaction, the star player's post-game smile, and the final score graphic over the network theme music (example: 4-5 slow-motion shots at ~4s each). Recommended framing: Curated 4-to-5 Shot Highlight & Emotion Sequence.
timing_constraint: Target window: 4-5 slow-motion shots at ~4s each. Ensure the final score graphic stays on screen through the fade to black.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Standing Spectator Blocking Sideline Camera Edge
trigger_condition: During an exciting late second-half possession, fans in the front row in front of CAM-1 (Main Wide) stand up and raise their arms into the very bottom edge of the camera frame. (Visual cue: Raised hands or heads of courtside spectators entering the bottom 10% of CAM-1 (Main Wide); Audio cue: Loud arena roar on a clutch three-point attempt.)
editor_action: Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) on air and slightly tighten or tilt upward by 1 to 2 degrees so the court and basket remain completely clear, never panic-cutting away from the main sideline angle during a live clutch shot (example: hold CAM-1 (Main Wide) despite minor bottom-edge spectator silhouettes). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: hold CAM-1 (Main Wide. Do not cut to a baseline camera while a live perimeter shot is in flight.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Foul-Out (5th Personal Foul) Takes Priority over Scorer Replay
trigger_condition: A star player commits their 5th personal foul (disqualifying them from the rest of the college game) on a play where the offensive player also made the layup. (Visual cue: Star player walking slowly toward the bench shaking their head as teammates tap their chest; Audio cue: Announcer states 'That is his fifth personal foul, he has fouled out of the game!'.)
editor_action: Prioritize the camera and graphics on the fouling-out star walking to the bench (showing their final points/rebounds/assists line) before rolling the replay of the layup, because a star's 5-foul disqualification changes the rest of the game (example: P2 Disqualification Storyline > P3 Routine Basket Replay). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) + Foul-Out Stat Banner.
timing_constraint: Still show a quick replay of the 5th foul call itself while the substitute checks in (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Celebrity / VIP Crowd Cutaway Eligibility Gate
trigger_condition: A camera operator spots a famous celebrity or former college legend sitting courtside and offers the shot to the director. (Visual cue: Courtside celebrity smiling or reacting to a play; Audio cue: Play-by-play announcer mentions who is in the building tonight.)
editor_action: Allow celebrity crowd cutaways only during full media timeouts, halftime, or routine non-clutch dead balls when no replay of a controversial call is pending and the game margin or clock is not in a high-tension clutch state (example: P5 Celebrity Cutaway permitted only when P1-P4 queues are empty). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Never cut to a celebrity in the crowd during the final 3 minutes of a close game.

title: Held-Ball Alternating Possession Arrow Graphic vs. Replay Arbitration
trigger_condition: Two players tie up the basketball for a held ball, triggering the NCAA alternating possession arrow. (Visual cue: Referees blowing the whistle, signaling a held ball with both thumbs up, and pointing in the direction of the possession arrow; Audio cue: Whistle and announcer calling 'Tie up! Possession arrow favors...'.)
editor_action: Show a quick 3-second replay of the physical tie-up while illuminating the alternating possession arrow indicator on the scorebug, then cut back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) before the referee hands the ball to the inbounder (example: ~3s tie-up replay + possession arrow highlight -> wide inbound). Recommended framing: Tight Scrap Replay (CAM-2, Baseline Low) -> Inbound Setup (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Never miss the live inbound pass after a held ball for a replay.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Coach 'Wired' Huddle Playback Placement Out of Timeout
trigger_condition: A full media timeout concludes and the broadcast returns from commercials with a cleared 7-second clip of the head coach speaking in the huddle. (Visual cue: Coach drawing on a dry-erase clipboard surrounded by seated players; Audio cue: Coach's motivational or tactical instructions.)
editor_action: Play the recorded 'Wired' coach huddle clip immediately upon returning from commercials while players are still walking back onto the court, then cut to CAM-1 (Main Wide) so the viewer can watch whether the team executes what the coach just asked for (example: ~7s huddle clip -> live first possession). Recommended framing: Bench Huddle Clip (CAM-4, Coach & Bench) -> Live Court (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~7s huddle clip -> live first possession. Always include closed-caption subtitles on the huddle clip.

title: Postgame Player-Of-The-Game & Final Stat Bookend
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern during the 30-to-60 second window after the final buzzer and handshake line.
editor_action: Transition from the handshake line on CAM-1 (Main Wide)/CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) to a CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) follow shot of the game's top performer alongside a full-screen 'Player of the Game' stat summary and a 3-clip game recap.
timing_constraint: Run during the 30s to 60s post-handshake wrap-up window.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Coach 'Mic'd up' Huddle Audio-Video Pairing
trigger_condition: Production plays a recorded 'Mic'd Up' audio clip of a head coach instructing players in the huddle coming out of a timeout.
editor_action: Lock the screen to CAM-4 (Coach/Bench Huddle) with a small 'Mic'd Up' speaker indicator while the coach's voice is playing, and hold off on showing unrelated stat banners so viewers can listen to the coach's strategy without reading competing text.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-4 with clean audio focus for the duration of the huddle clip and return to CAM-1 before the throw-in (example: 8s to 12s huddle clip).

title: One-Banner-Per-Stoppage Cap (Preventing Back-To-Back Graphic Clutter)
trigger_condition: Two different stat milestones happen on the same play before a whistle (for example, a player hits 20 points AND records their 5th assist).
editor_action: Never flash two separate lower-third banners back-to-back during the same short whistle pause. Display only the single highest-priority banner (or merge both stats onto one two-line card) and save the secondary stat for the next stoppage.
timing_constraint: Maximum 1 lower-third graphic card per dead-ball whistle stoppage (Resolve priority conflict within < 0.2s; P1 Live Ball always preempts lower-tier requests.)

title: Rim-Protector & Shot-Blocker Paint Deterrence Arc
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a center or power forward blocks 2+ shots or alters multiple drives in the painted lane.
editor_action: After the 2nd blocked shot, cue a two-clip CAM-5 (Above-Rim) Above-Rim replay package showing how the rim protector is forcing opponents to settle for outside jump shots.
timing_constraint: Roll during the next whistle pause after a player's 2nd or 3rd block (example: 6.5s package).
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Blowout vs. Competitive Game Pacing Shift (20+ Point Margin Rule)
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when the score margin exceeds 20 points in the final 8 minutes of the second half.
editor_action: Shift from high-tension crunch-time pacing to storytelling mode: feature bench reserves checking in on CAM-3, show wider season/tournament context graphics, and allow full celebratory holds on bench-player baskets.
timing_constraint: Activate relaxed storytelling cadence when lead >= 20 points with < 08:00 remaining (Evaluate across rolling 4-minute media segments and return to CAM-1 before live throw-ins.)

title: Explaining Why an Offensive Charge Does Not Give Free Throws
trigger_condition: An offensive player commits a charging foul or illegal screen while the opposing team is already in the Bonus (7+ team fouls).
editor_action: Because casual viewers often expect free throws on every foul once a team is in the Bonus, flash a clear scoreboard note ('Offensive Foul: Turnover, No Free Throws Awarded') as play reverses direction.
timing_constraint: Flash 3.0s turnover clarification pill during the side-out handoff.
plain_english_tip: Bonus rule: At 7+ team fouls in a half, opponents shoot 1-and-1 free throws; at 10+ fouls (Double Bonus), they get 2 automatic free throws.

title: Over-And-Back (Backcourt Violation) Plain-English Explanation
trigger_condition: An offensive team brings the ball across the mid-court line into the frontcourt, and then touches the ball in the backcourt again without a defender deflecting it.
editor_action: Trigger a brief scoreboard explanation ('Backcourt Violation: Ball Cannot Cross Back Over Mid-Court Line') while keeping CAM-1 (Main Wide) framed on the mid-court turnover spot.
timing_constraint: Display 3.0s rule note during the mid-court throw-in setup.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Kicked-Ball Violation Shot-Clock Reset Rule (20 Seconds vs. Keep Current Time)
trigger_condition: A defender intentionally kicks or blocks a pass with their foot/leg, stopping play.
editor_action: Explain why the offense gets the ball back out of bounds: if the shot clock was below 20 seconds, it resets to 20; if it was at 20 or higher, it stays where it was.
timing_constraint: Flash 'Kicked Ball: Shot Clock Reset to 20s' on the scoreboard during the throw-in.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Basket Interference vs. Offensive Put-Back Rule
trigger_condition: An offensive player touches the ball or pulls on the rim while the ball is directly inside the imaginary cylinder above the hoop.
editor_action: Cue a CAM-5 (Above-Rim) replay looking straight down into the hoop and display 'Offensive Basket Interference: No Basket' so viewers see why the tip-dunk was waved off.
timing_constraint: 4.0s CAM-5 overhead replay during the dead-ball turnover.
plain_english_tip: Goaltending: Defenders cannot swat a shot once it is on its downward arc toward the hoop; doing so awards automatic points.

title: 2-For-1 End-Of-Half Clock Math (35 to 45 Seconds Remaining)
trigger_condition: With 35 to 45 seconds remaining in the 1st Half, the team with the ball pushes quickly to shoot before ~32 seconds left on the game clock.
editor_action: Flash a '2-for-1 Opportunity' note on the scoreboard explaining that shooting before 32 seconds guarantees the team will get the ball back one more time before halftime because the shot clock is 30 seconds.
timing_constraint: Display when the offense has the ball between 42.0s and 33.0s left in the 1st Half.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Double Technical / Offset Foul Explanation (No Free Throws, Resume at Point of Interruption)
trigger_condition: Two opposing players get tangled up and referees call a 'double foul' or 'double technical foul' on both players.
editor_action: Because the two penalties cancel each other out, flash a clear scoreboard banner ('Offsetting Double Fouls: Penalties Cancel, Ball Awarded at Point of Interruption') so viewers know why nobody shoots free throws.
timing_constraint: Display for 5.0s after the referee announces the offsetting calls.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Handling 'Turnovers' and 30-Second Shot-Clock Violations
trigger_condition: The offense loses the ball to the other team ('a turnover') by throwing a bad pass out of bounds, taking too many steps without dribbling ('traveling'), or failing to hit the rim before the 30-second shot timer expires.
editor_action: If the defense steals the ball during live play, stay locked on CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide for the fast break. If a whistle stops play for traveling or an expired 30-second shot timer, show a quick reaction of the rugged defensive stop on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) and update the team's forced-turnover count on the scoreboard before the throw-in.
timing_constraint: Instant wide hold on live steals; brief defensive celebration cut + turnover stat note on dead-ball violations (example: 2.2s defensive reaction).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Explaining 3-Second Lane, 5-Second Inbound, and 10-Second Backcourt Whistle Rules
trigger_condition: A referee blows the whistle and awards the ball to the other team because of a time-limit violation rather than physical contact.
